claim_summary: The fallback construction yields 59 event clusters, of which 53 support the five-class endpoint.
The grouped evaluation contains 46 embargo groups across three outer folds.
The released Phase-2 inputs contain 1004 attack-labeled network observations and 283 timestamped provenance observations.
The post-hoc host-link audit finds 8077 usable process-socket observations and 755 endpoint/time matches within 0.1 s.
The author-mapped Ubuntu VM1 endpoint receives 733 corroborating socket/flow matches and occurs in all 1004 attack-labeled network rows.
The host-link-supported cohort contains 33 events, 32 in-support events, and 31 evaluated non-pilot events.
The released-file audit finds no usable malicious-process socket-to-flow match and does not independently verify a packet-to-PID causal join.
Stage A uses 69 network-window features.
Stage B uses 55 typed process features and excludes identity features.
At the primary Stage-A budget, HGB reaches window AP 0.844 and all-event coverage 0.697 with 0.134 observed false alerts per hour.
Across four Stage-A budgets, coverage rises from 0.697 to 0.800 while observed false alerts rise from 0.134 to 1.830 per hour.
The corresponding retained timestamped-provenance byte fraction rises from 0.300 to 0.385.
Typed Logistic retrieval reaches 0.952 midrank MRR and 0.949 expected-tie Recall at one.
Candidate graphs have minimum 7, median 14, mean 285.39, and maximum 8924 processes.
Retrieval MRR across small, medium, and large candidate-pool strata is 0.993, 0.875, and 0.750.
Retrieval radii of 60, 300, and 900 seconds yield truth ceilings of 0.881, 0.983, and 1.000.
Across ten grouped split seeds, retrieval MRR is 0.940 plus or minus 0.022.
Process-family holdout retains approximately 0.93 MRR and 0.92 Recall at one.
Removing process semantics lowers retrieval to approximately 0.69 MRR and 0.52 Recall at one.
The full-coverage tactic classifier reaches 0.623 accuracy and 0.399 macro-F1.
The fold-local majority baseline labels 26 of 53 events correctly at full coverage.
The joint endpoint-seeded pruning rule excludes the truth process in all 11 cases in which it activates.
At fixed 42-of-53 acceptance, controller risk is 0.381 and posterior-margin risk is 0.310.
The deletion score provides only 0.032 average truth-removal lift.
The frozen LLM study contains 954 outputs and both prespecified hypotheses fail.
The first LLM hypothesis yields a 0.039 corruption-macro wrong-label reduction, below its 0.05 target.
The second LLM hypothesis yields 0.588 clean coverage with a 0.216 coverage gap and fails its coverage conditions.
At deployable thresholds EviGate-Bind accepts 33 clean events, labels 25 correctly, and labels 8 wrongly.
At deployable thresholds posterior margin accepts 38 clean events, labels 28 correctly, and labels 10 wrongly.
Deployable EviGate-Bind and margin have five-family corruption wrong-label rates of 0.114 and 0.278.
Deployable EviGate-Bind and margin have context-replacement wrong-label rates of 0.333 and 0.882.
At matched clean acceptance, the five-family wrong-label reduction is 0.141 with interval 0.102 to 0.180.
Removing posterior-level network features adds 12 of 51 context errors.
Network-only and provenance-only controls each add 14 of 51 context errors.
The no-LLM cascade has the same clean outcomes as the full cascade.
The LLM incremental three-family reduction is 0.026 with interval minus 0.007 to 0.065; this is not an equivalence result.
Among accepted foreign packages the full cascade has 0.944 selective risk.
Same-tactic-only negative training retains 74.1 percent of the full context-replacement gain.
Natural evidence overlap occurs in 13 of 46 embargo groups, covering 26 events and 13 pairs; 11 pairs have bidirectional truth overlap.
End-to-end accounting gives 15 Stage-A misses, 12 unattributed events, 24 attributed events, and 18 correct labels.
The truth process is present in the top-ten package for 11 of 12 unattributed alerts; the exception ranks 8901 of 8924.
On the 31-event host-link-supported subset EviGate-Bind has 22 accepted, 18 correct, and 4 wrong clean outcomes.
On the same subset EviGate-Bind produces 7 context-replacement wrong labels versus 25 for matched margin.
EviGate-Bind has lower decision cost than calibrated margin when abstention costs less than 0.40 of a wrong label.
Compact top-ten packages occupy 0.0327 of full-graph serialized bytes; post-decision acceptance does not reduce acquisition needs.
The CPU cascade has 2.64-ms median and 3.83-ms p95 wall time over 306 measurements on the stated server-class CPU.
The maintained repository exposes 130 executable unit tests, including the submission claim audit.
The study evaluates within-campaign compatibility-aware triage; direct packet-to-PID causality and cross-campaign generalization are outside its evaluation.
Figure 3 reports foreign-context, five-family, and clean-risk paired effects of 0.529, 0.141, and 0.091.
The dataset-independent benchmark contract specifies alert, process, split, evidence, corruption, output, and reproducibility requirements.
The frozen Stage C confusion matrix contains 33 correct predictions among 53 in-support events.
The post-freeze BindGate score has descriptive clean-versus-foreign AUROC 0.692 on 51 paired packages.
The fixed-threshold signed clock-offset audit changes the clean operating point at 30-second offsets and requires time alignment.
A post-freeze synthetic Phase-1 busy-window stress adds median 80 benign process candidates and yields Stage-B MRR 0.783 and R@10 0.915 over 59 held-out events.
Across five deterministic benign-window assignments, busy-window Stage-B MRR ranges from 0.760 to 0.849 without retraining.
The dataset author's thesis maps 172.16.63.128 to Ubuntu VM1 and 172.16.65.128 to Kali VM1; 172.16.67.128 is Raspberry Pi2.
The released Caldera attack-information file contains 58 distinct PIDs, all found as attack-labeled Process entities in VM1 provenance.
Every Caldera timestamp has a same-tactic network attack record within 30 seconds; this is campaign-level corroboration, not a packet-to-PID join.
Only one of 45 non-cleanup Caldera time/PID pairs has a provenance process time within 60 seconds of its own row, so the file is not substituted for the frozen 59-cluster manifest.
The dataset author describes Caldera-PID provenance labeling and timestamp/IP-calibrated packet-level network labeling as separate procedures.
